extracted.intended_audience: essayists, periodical writers, and members of learned societies (e.g., contributors to daily/pamphlet essays and compilers of natural history)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and publishing short, periodical essays (single-sheet/short papers) and for compiling concise natural-history species accounts; covers style, structure, audience, and format choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate engagement and lively treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must immediately fall into our Subject, and treat every Part of it in a lively Manner,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-sheet essays cannot rely on long preambles; each paper must begin promptly and maintain a lively tone throughout so readers do not discard it as dull or insipid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matter must lie close together; novelty or striking expression
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our Matter must lie close together, and either be wholly new in itself, or in the Turn it receives from our Expressions,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of limited space and large readership, content should be concentrated and either substantively new or presented with an original phrasing/angle to engage readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each sheet should be a compact treatise (completeness of thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: "every Sheet should be a kind of Treatise, and make out in Thought what it wants in Bulk,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although short, each essay should present a coherent, self-contained argument or exploration — the thoughtfulness of a longer piece compressed into a brief form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work up a point of humour in all its parts
rubrics_metrics.description: "That a Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the essay aims to be humorous, the comic point must be fully developed within the piece — do not leave humour fragmentary or only hinted at.

rubrics_metrics.name: Touch the subject on essential articles; avoid repetition and enlargement
rubrics_metrics.description: "A Subject touched upon in its most essential Articles, without the Repetitions, Tautologies and Enlargements, that are indulged to longer Labours,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be economical: cover just the essential aspects and avoid the repetitive expansions acceptable in longer volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distill the work (Chymical Method): give the virtue of a full draught in few drops
rubrics_metrics.description: "An Essay-Writer must practise in the Chymical Method, and give the Virtue of a full Draught in a few Drops,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for concentrated potency — convey the effect and insight of a long piece in a highly condensed form (metaphorically like distilling a medicine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt style to publication format (volume vs separate sheets)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A Man who publishes his Works in a Volume, has an infinite Advantage... those who publish their Thoughts in distinct Sheets... have none of these Advantages,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format deliberately: volumes permit digressions and allowances for dullness, whereas separate papers demand immediacy, compactness, and liveliness; adjust tone and structure accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting — do not write for 'Moles' (those incapable or hostile)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is not therefore for the Benefit of Moles that I publish these my daily Essays,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conscious of audience capacity and disposition; aim to instruct and amuse readers capable of appreciating the work rather than pandering to the ignorant or envious; accept that some readers will be unreceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and accept author-to-author envy and hostile critics
rubrics_metrics.description: "One Author is a Mole to another Author... They can indeed see the Light... but immediately shut their Eyes... and withdraw themselves into a wilful Obscurity,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that other writers may focus on blemishes rather than beauties; this is a social reality of publishing and should not dictate the writer's choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure for natural-history species accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the several Writers among them took each his particular Species, and gave us a distinct Account of its Original, Birth and Education; its Policies, Hostilities and Alliances, with the Frame and Texture of its inward and outward Parts, and particularly those that distinguish it from all other Animals, with their peculiar Aptitudes for the State of Being in which Providence has placed them,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling natural history, each species account should be systematic: origin and birth, upbringing/education, social/predatory relationships, anatomy (internal and external), distinguishing features, and special adaptations — i.e., a comprehensive but focused species dossier.
